fixes.explanation: Right, baker. After the sons bring the fat portions from the ox and the ram, the text says they “placed these on the breasts.” (Leviticus 9:19-20). Then Aaron burns the fat portions on the altar. The fat gets a ride on top of the breasts before it ever sees the fire.

Pack the bags, friend? Not this time. Moses gives Aaron a different message to pass on: “For today the LORD will appear to you.” (Leviticus 9:4). No move is mentioned in these verses. All of those offerings are about the LORD showing up, and I'd say that's plenty of reason to get the dough ready.

Right, baker. Fire came out from the presence of the LORD and consumed “the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar.” (Leviticus 9:24). The fire comes from the LORD's presence. When all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown. I think that moment is one to stand still and take in.
